[BSP reconstruction 0041dd40]
If desired length unchanged do nothing; zero desired length releases old data through00419cc0/00bd1510 and clears both fields. Nonzero new length allocates length+1 through00419cc0/00bd1120, optionally copies min(old,new), returns old storage if nonnull, writes newlength/data and trailing zero byte. Resolver invokes from zeroed fresh output so old storage is absent. Original ABI: ECX8-byte string; stack desired unsigned length and preserve flag (low byte); RET8. Evidence: docs/VERTEX_FORMAT_RESOLUTION.md; reports/mesh_declaration_resolver_audit.json. Descriptive symbol is a hypothesis. Host projection is not native ABI or gameplay validation.

[BSP reconstruction 0041dd40] update
Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet app_init_alloc_string_helpers, assembly-verified. __thiscall, ECX 8-byte string {uint length +0, char* data +4}, stack (uint length, char preserve), RET 8. No capacity field, no small-buffer area: the block is always length+1 bytes, so a shrink reallocates. A request for the length already held returns immediately even when data is null (0041dd4a). Length 0 releases data with old_length+1 and clears both fields. Otherwise it allocates length+1 from the string pool (00419cc0 then 00bd1120) BEFORE releasing the old block, optionally copies min(old,new) bytes, releases the old block with old_length+1, then stores data/length and writes the terminator at data[length]. 2280 callers. Evidence: docs/APP_INIT_ALLOC_STRINGS.md.
